correspondence.finding: The southern selected beginning lies in the Mana headwater setting west of Saül and north of Mont Galbao. The Saül sheet shows its northward connection through the Repentir and upper-river setting, then the east-west bends toward Saut Tambour, Saut Magloire and the river printed Mana. The nearby Saint-Eloi, Sophie and other criques remain separately labeled waterways; their names are not transferred to the complete mainstem. The precise official source point and names of each small headwater feeder are not established.

Between the northern edge of the Saül sheet and the southern edge of the Trinité sheet, the retained whole-Guyane park drainage map shows a continuous Mana trunk, with Eau Blanche approaching from the west and Loubère from the east. This readable connection bridges the two anchored parts without a competing trunk or a name transfer onto either tributary. The bridge is supported at coarser regional scale than the surrounding sheets; individual bends and feeder heads are not separately resolved.

The middle selected corridor matches the Mana west of the Montagnes de la Trinité: the river runs north from the Pakira setting past Roche Cabrit and the Ikissi, Aïmara and Baboune rapid sequence toward Saut Fracas and Bois Couronné. Crique Forte and the separate eastern Kokioko drainage remain distinguishable from this main river. Local bends and rapids are generalized by the model.

Near Bon Espoir the Mana approaches from the southeast, turns north, receives the Arouani from the south, and then receives Crique Lézard from the west farther downstream. The sole selected tributary follows only the short lower northward Arouani approach to the first junction. The report's regional and detailed maps distinguish that approach from Crique Lézard, Crique Mousse and the more distant Kokioko. The entire Arouani basin and its upstream source are not selected.

The lower selected Mana continues north through the bend sequence toward Saut Tamanoir and Saut Sabbat, then past Angoulême, Terre Rouge and Mana bourg. The municipal map separates this river from Crique Portal and the Acarouany approach, and from the Maroni farther west. These nearby tributaries are context, not additional selected paths.

The selection continues northwest beyond Mana bourg into the coastal approach. Its generalized endpoint is not sufficient to establish the present ocean-mouth position, the full westward estuarine extension or an administrative sea limit. The older cartography is used for river identity and approach only; no precise modern shoreline or tidal boundary is claimed.

correspondence: The one selected mainstem piece and its full extent were inspected. It begins in the southern interior, runs north along a long western leg, bends northeast to its northernmost interior section, then turns east through several broad model bends before descending southeast and ending after a short eastward lower segment. No separate tributary fragment is selected.

The western and northern route lies within the mapped Inland Ice. Its eastward and southeastward continuation approaches the southeastern glaciated margin in the broader inland Køge Bugt region. The readable graticule, continuous ice field, ice contours and adjacent coast support this whole-route feature-class reading. The endpoint is not assigned to a specific glacier, fjord or marginal stream.

No natural river hydronym is established for the whole modeled ice-sheet path. A nearby glacier, settlement or fjord label cannot name the full selection. This positive feature-class mismatch is a completed naming-scope hold, not a claim that all marginal streams lack names or a report of missing source material.

The map legend distinguishes ice-surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments south of 68°N. These map symbols do not prove named-river flow or a present-day surface or subglacial connection along the modeled path.

correspondence.finding: The northern modeled approach passes south through the Holden–Jessamine–Conway urban-lake setting. Orange County maps and flowpath descriptions distinguish these lakes and their controls: Holden is listed as landlocked with drainwells and a separate overflow relationship toward Jessamine; Jessamine has an eastern weir/pipe/channel connection to Conway; Conway has a controlled southeastern outlet toward Lake Marie Prairie. These support a connected drainage setting at regional scale, not one uninterrupted natural stream name. The brief initial urban approach has no verified individual channel name in this assessment and is not asserted to be an official river source. Exact lake-shore and infrastructure intersections are not inferred from the generalized path.

South of the urban lake/outlet setting, the selected approach follows the Boggy Creek/swamp corridor toward the northwestern side of East Lake Tohopekaliga. The basin map and upper navigation map distinguish this from Shingle Creek farther west and from the Hart/Mary Jane/Fells Cove approach east of it. Boggy Creek is a component hydronym; the full set of upstream urban lakes and outlets is not renamed Boggy Creek merely because it lies in that drainage basin.

The route crosses the East Lake Tohopekaliga setting, takes the C-31/S-59 connection westward into Lake Tohopekaliga, then continues via the southern S-61/C-35 corridor to Cypress Lake. It then follows the C-36/Hatchineha and C-37/Kissimmee chain before leaving Lake Kissimmee at S-65. The original upper-basin map labels these waterbodies and connectors separately. The model line through a lake does not turn the lake into a natural river reach or establish a surveyed navigation route.

From Lake Kissimmee the selected southward corridor agrees with the lower-basin map’s Kissimmee River/C-38 alignment, including the upper straightened reach, central restored/meandering-river setting, Basinger/lower structures and the final approach to Okee-Tantie at Lake Okeechobee. Istokpoga, Harney Pond and Indian Prairie routes join from separate western directions and are not selected tributary fragments. The historical map’s restoration phases are kept separate from any claim about the present flow channel.

After the Kissimmee inflow, the model continues within the northern/western Lake Okeechobee setting and toward the western-lake approach to Moore Haven. The acquired brochure distinguishes the lake from its northern inflows, the Caloosahatchee western outlet and the St. Lucie eastern outlet. The modeled interior-lake arc and westward connection are not independently named as Kissimmee River, a rim canal, or a marked Okeechobee Waterway route. The fragment boundary inside this lake/western-margin setting does not establish a hydronym boundary.

The continuation turns through the Moore Haven/S-77 outlet sector and west through the Lake Hicpochee/C-43 corridor, passing the Ortona/S-78, LaBelle, Alva and Franklin/S-79 settings. The historical SFWMD plan expressly treats C-43 and Caloosahatchee River together while describing artificial connection, excavation and channel modification. These are supported local river/canal designations, not evidence that the name extends north through Lake Okeechobee to Orlando. Nearby C-19, agricultural canals, sloughs and Orange River remain separate features.

The last selected reach continues west of the Franklin/Olga vicinity in the lower Caloosahatchee corridor and ends before central Fort Myers. The SFWMD plan’s regional maps cover the river farther downstream, allowing the selected endpoint to be distinguished from the full estuary and Gulf outlet. The modeled endpoint is not identified as the river’s official mouth.

The western selected beginning follows the drainage through the El Ermitaño reservoir setting near Quebrada Arriba, then bends southeast and east across the western Torres lowlands toward Carora. Andrade and colleagues' Figure 7 independently maps this connected western drainage and distinguishes the more southerly reservoir systems. Neither a reservoir polygon nor every neighboring feeder is included merely because the line crosses this setting.

The connected selected route turns northeast at Carora and follows the Morere valley past Aregue to the Río Tocuyo settlement/confluence setting. The MOP map prints Río Morere along this valley and shows the receiving Tocuyo approach separately. The selected western continuation is therefore not evidence that the Tocuyo itself originates at the western model endpoint.

After the tributary connection, the selection follows the receiving river north toward Siquisique and then east along the elongated middle-basin corridor. Its later northeast turn and lower coastward course agree with the entire-basin map in the 2007 field study. That map separates the Baragua, Urama, Araurima and other side drainages rather than combining them into the selected line.

The northeastern ending is in the lower Tocuyo coastward approach. The study separates its final coastal reach from the nearby Játira–Tacarigua waterbody and Golfete de Cuare. The selection is not extended into those waterbodies or treated as a complete present-day estuary or marine-mouth outline.

The southern upper Tocuyo, Dos Cerritos, Atarigua, the complete Los Quediches and Puricaure reservoir systems, and the many unselected tributaries remain separate. The western connecting reach can remain partly unnamed while its connection to the supported Morere–Tocuyo route is recorded. No hydronym is transferred from a nearby or inconsistently placed label.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
